free_tier.stated: 100 free hours of a 1 GB machine in the first 30 days, with no card.

per_object_cap.stated: free tier caps a sandbox at 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 10 GiB disk; a paid account goes to 16 vCPU / 64 GiB / 400 GiB

retention.stated: A paused sandbox keeps files and memory at USD 0.08 per decimal GB per 30-day month; a snapshot or a custom image costs the same.

egress.terms: 100 GiB a month of outbound traffic is free, then USD 0.02/GB; inbound traffic is free.

limits.value: outbound traffic 100 GiB a month free, then USD 0.02/GB
a dedicated IPv4 address is USD 5 per 30-day month and a WireGuard tunnel is USD 5 per 30-day month, so there is no free public port

identity_cost.detail: 100 free hours with no card; a paid account needs a payment method whose type and hold were not stated on the pricing page. Unverified for the paid path.

reliability_note: Compute has no one-minute minimum and memory bills only while compute runs; waiting is charged at a 50-millicore CPU floor.
confidence_note: Both usage rates, the idle floor, the free allowance, the add-on prices and the paused-sandbox rate are quoted from the pricing page read today. What would raise it: the exact bill for a machine kept running with no work, which the vendor models but does not publish.

evidence.proved: 'Free usage: 100 free hours of a 1 GB machine in your first 30 days, no card' with '$0.025 per active vCPU-hour', '$0.0075 per reserved GiB-hour', 'Outbound traffic: 100 GiB a month free, then $0.02 per GB', 'Compute has no one-minute minimum, and memory is billed while compute runs', and the measured comparison '1,000 one-minute runs of 2 vCPU, 4 GiB: Runtime $0.64 against Fly Machines $1.53', quoted
quoted: 'Active CPU | $0.025 per active vCPU-hour'; 'Memory | $0.0075 per reserved GiB-hour'; '100 free hours of a 1 GB machine in your first 30 days, no card'
quoted: 'Waiting means memory plus the default CPU floor of 50 millicores, a twentieth of a vCPU.'
quoted: 'Dedicated IPv4 address | $5 per 30-day month'; 'WireGuard tunnel, up to 16 peers | $5 per 30-day month'

notes: The dossier's existing record is `trial-only` with no m24h. The arithmetic at 24/7 for 1 GiB sitting idle: 0.05 vCPU x 0.025 + 1 GiB x 0.0075 = USD 0.00875/hour x 730 = USD 6.39. Busy at 1 vCPU: 0.025 + 0.0075 = USD 0.0325/hour x 730 = USD 23.73. Either way over USD 5, and the free tier is 100 hours, not a month. Egress: USD 0.02/GB x 1000 = USD 20 per TB beyond the 100 GiB allowance. Note the vendor's own framing (42% to 88% cheaper) is measured against agents that wait on a model, not against an always-on box, which is why the 730-hour figure is the one that decides.

shape.note: 1 GiB with the 50-millicore default CPU floor while waiting
